'''Puri''' ({{Langx|prr|Kwaytikindo|links=no}} 'language'<ref name=":2" />) is an [[Extinct language|extinct]] and revitalizing language of eastern [[Brazil]], spoken by the [[Puri people]]. It ceased being spoken sometime in the 19th century, but the Puri people have reconstructed the language, and a number of second-language speakers exist, according to the ''[[Ethnologue]]''.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Puri Language (PRR) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use {{!}} Ethnologue Free |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/prr/ |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=Ethnologue (Free All) |language=en}}</ref> It can be considered a language isolate, with the related [[Coroado Puri dialect|Coroado language]] seen as a dialect.

== Geographical distribution ==
Puri was spoken in a continuous region stretching from the [[Preto River (São Paulo)|Preto River]] to the [[Paraíba do Sul|Paraíba River]] (from [[Queluz, São Paulo]] to [[Paraibuna]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]). The Puri occupied the Upper [[Paraíba do Sul River]] up to [[Queluz, São Paulo]], and the Coroado from the [[Pomba River]] to the [[Doce River]] in [[Minas Gerais]].<ref name="Ramirez">{{Cite journal |last=Ramirez |first=Henri |last2=Vegini |first2=Valdir |last3=França |first3=Maria Cristina Victorino de |date=2015-09-26 |title=Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste Brasileiro |url=http://periodicos.sbu.unicamp.br/ojs/index.php/liames/article/view/8642302 |journal=LIAMES: Línguas Indígenas Americanas |language=pt |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=223–277 |doi=10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302 |issn=2177-7160|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Classification ==
Puri and Coroado (sometimes collectively called ''Purian'') may be related to [[Waitaká language|Waitaká]], which is unattested. Previously, the [[Koropó language]], once spoken in [[Minas Gerais]] and [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]], was seen as Purian by Loukotka (1935),<ref name=":1">{{cite thesis |last1=Neto |first1=Ambrósio Pereira da Silva |title=Revisão da Classificaçao Da Família Lingüística Puri |date=2007 |page=23 |url=http://www.etnolinguistica.org/local--files/tese:silva-2007/Dissert_Ambrosio%20Pereira%20da%20Silva%20Neto.pdf |access-date=23 November 2022}}</ref> but it has been proven to be part of the [[Maxakalían languages]] instead by Ramirez et al. (2015).<ref name="Ramirez" /><ref>{{Citation |last=Campbell |first=Lyle |title=Indigenous Languages of South America |date=2024-06-25 |work=The Indigenous Languages of the Americas |pages=182–279 |url=https://academic.oup.com/book/57386/chapter-abstract/464719092?redirectedFrom=fulltext |access-date=2025-04-21 |edition=1 |publisher=Oxford University PressNew York |language=en |doi=10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0004 |isbn=978-0-19-767346-1|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Purian was initially part of the [[Macro-Jê]] proposal. However, when Coropó is removed, there are not sufficient lexical connections to maintain this classification.<ref>{{cite web| editor-last1= Hammarström| editor-first1 = Harald| editor-last2 = Forke| editor-first2 = Robert| editor-last3 = Haspelmath| editor-first3 = Martin| editor-last4 = Bank| editor-first4 = Sebastian| year = 2020|title = Puri-Coroado | work = [[Glottolog]] 4.3| url = https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/puri1261}}</ref>

The [[Waitaká language|Waitaká]] and Maromomin languages, both extinct, are possibly belonging to the Purian family, but this is not confirmable as no linguistic information was recorded.<ref name="Loukotka">{{cite book |last=Loukotka |first=Čestmír |author-link=Čestmír Loukotka |title=Classification of South American Indian languages |url=https://archive.org/details/classificationof0007louk |url-access=registration |publisher=UCLA Latin American Center |year=1968 |location=Los Angeles}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Dixon |first=Robert M. W. |title=The Amazonian languages |last2=Aikhenvald |first2=Alexandra Y. |date=1999 |publisher=Cambridge university press |isbn=978-0-521-57021-3 |series=Cambridge language surveys |location=Cambridge (GB) |page=166}}</ref>

== History ==
In the 2010s, a Puri language revitalization project was launched in the indigenous village of Maraká’nà (Maracanã), [[Rio de Janeiro State]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Puri |first1=Txâma Xambé |last2=Puri |first2=Tutushamum |last3=Puri |first3=Xindêda |date=2021-01-20 |title=Kwaytikindo: retomada linguística Puri |url=https://periodicos.unifap.br/index.php/linguasindigenas/article/view/6311 |journal=Revista Brasileira de Línguas Indígenas |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=77 |doi=10.18468/rbli.2020v3n2.p77-101 |issn=2595-685X|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2021, a primer was published.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Gamito |first=José Aristides Silva |date=2021-01-01 |title=Cartilha da Língua Puri - um exercício de revitalização |url=https://www.academia.edu/63126955}}</ref>
